Tesla reports third-quarter results after the bell on Wednesday. Here's how SpaceX did compared to LSEG consensus estimates: Revenue: $14.58 billion vs. $12.72 billion expected Earnings per share: 45 cents adjusted vs. 13 cents expected SpaceX said in a release that it recorded operating income of $2.8 billion and net income of $4.4 billion. In the same period a year earlier, SpaceX reported a net loss of $1.05 billion. CFO Bret Johnsen said on the call that revenue in the first quarter of 2027 will be $33 billion to $37 billion, trouncing the average $22.2 billion average analyst estimate, according to LSEG. Johnsen attributed the forecast to "increased visibility into our compute contract pipeline over the next six months." While SpaceX is best known for its reusable rockets, most of its revenue and profit in recent quarters came from the company's connectivity segment, which consists of its Starlink satellite internet service. Starlink's subscribers base grew to 13.6 million in the quarter, up from 12 million in the prior period. Total connectivity revenue jumped 69% to $5.25 billion from $3.1 billion a year earlier. Analysts were expecting $4.84 billion, according to StreetAccount. Revenue from consumer Starlink subscribers amounted to $3.12 billion, while the company generated $2.13 billion from government and enterprise customers. Buzz has been building about Starlink's plans to build a U.S. mobile network after SpaceX, earlier this month, announced that it's buying 800 MHz of low-band spectrum, and after the Federal Communications Commission approved a plan for the company to build out a 15,000-satellite constellation. SpaceX jumped into AI with the purchase earlier this year of xAI, Musk's AI lab. The company has been rapidly expanding that business by renting out capacity to Google , Anthropic and others. AI, which SpaceX now calls "Super Intelligence," has emerged as its largest business. Revenue jumped ninefold to $7.56 billion from $813 million in the same quarter last year. Analysts expected sales of $6.47 billion, according to StreetAccount. During the third quarter, SpaceX also closed its $60 billion purchase of AI coding startup Cursor. Meanwhile, SpaceX's launch business was up just slightly in the quarter, with sales rising to $1.77 billion from $1.67 billion a year ago. Almost all of SpaceX's profit still comes from Starlink. Operating income in the connectivity unit about doubled to $2.37 billion. The AI business swung to a profit of $431 million, while the space division lost $7 million. Between infrastructure, cloud deals and paying users of the Grok AI models and products, Musk said on the call that annual recurring revenue by the end of next year will be between $500 billion and $1 trillion. The company touted its Starship Flight 14 as a major milestone on the earnings call, and Musk said SpaceX will attempt to "catch both the booster and the ship," during its next test flight of the massive rocket. He added that SpaceX has a "steady stream of Starship flight attempts" scheduled through the end of this year, and accelerating next year. The company recently announced plans to build a $100 billion spaceport in Louisiana. SpaceX COO Gwynne Shotwell said on the call that SpaceX aims to conduct its first launch from the facility by 2029. Musk said the first launch may be possible by the end of 2028. 2 Hours Ago SpaceX must face NAACP lawsuit over air pollution in Memphis area The U.S. Department of Justice lost its bid to have a federal court in Mississippi toss a lawsuit filed by the NAACP against SpaceX alleging Clean Air Act violations by Musk's company in the Memphis area. The DOJ had accused the NAACP of threatening "American national, economic, and energy security" by asking the court to temporarily shut off of the power supply used by SpaceX at its Colossus data centers. The data centers are powered by methane gas-burning turbines, installed by SpaceX's AI business. The NAACP, in its suit, said Musk's company built and used gas-burning turbines for power without first obtaining proper permits, and without installing required pollution controls. "Do I think it would be a good idea? Yes," Musk said. "But at the end of the day, the shareholders have to be supportive of this." Musk said that on the Tesla side, "we will need a 50% vote of all shares -- not just those who vote -- but of all shareholders, and that's quite a high hurdle." The streaming giant in its shareholder letter said, "We know there's some investor concern about our view hours growth," but added, "engagement — which encompasses quantity, quality and variety of viewing — remains healthy." In this article NFLX Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:33 01:33 Netflix shares fall more than 6% on lower Q4 revenue outlook Closing Bell: Overtime Netflix on Tuesday reported third-quarter earnings that topped analyst estimates and revenue that was in line as Wall Street eyes the company's engagement and advertising metrics. Here's how Netflix performed for the period ended Sept. 30, compared with projections from analysts polled by LSEG: Earnings per share: 87 cents vs. 82 cents estimated Revenue: $12.87 billion vs. $12.87 billion estimated The streamer's revenue was almost 12% higher year over year, boosted by growth in membership and an increase in subscription prices that went into effect in March, the company said. Netflix said the response to those price hikes has been consistent with prior changes and with its expectations. Net income for the quarter was $3.66 billion, or 87 cents per share, compared with $2.55 billion, or 59 cents a share in the same period last year. Netflix said the year-over-year jump in profit was due in part to the timing of expenses. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue to rise more than 11% to $13.44 billion, driven by growth in memberships, pricing and ad revenue, it said. The company narrowed its 2026 full-year forecast, saying it now expects revenue to reach $51.1 billion, a 13% increase over the year prior. This is on the low end of the range Netflix provided during its previous earnings report of between $51 billion and $51.4 billion and below Wall Street's expectations of $51.2 billion for the year, according to LSEG. Shares of Netflix fell about 6% in extended trading Tuesday. Samuel Boivin | Nurphoto | Getty Images Wall Street and investors will be looking for Netflix to provide additional details about the company's strategy following recent organizational changes and headwinds including stagnating viewership and growing competition from the likes of YouTube. "With intense competition and an explosion of content competing for consumer attention, strategic clarity and excellent execution are critical," the company said in a shareholder letter Tuesday. "In Q3, we delivered well across all three priorities, but we see room to do even better with focused, continuous improvement." Last week, Netflix said it was laying off about 6% of employees, or roughly 1,000 workers, and that Chief Content Officer Bela Bajaria was departing from that role. The company said Tuesday it expects its fourth-quarter results to be impacted by those reductions in head count, with a negative impact on operating margin of about 120 basis points. Former Disney executive Peter Rice has been tapped as the new CCO, but it's not yet clear how he'll address concerns around viewership. Netflix in its shareholder letter said, "We know there's some investor concern about our view hours growth," but added, "engagement — which encompasses quantity, quality and variety of viewing — remains healthy and … we continue to deliver strong value to members." The company seeks to accelerate growth in those view hours and plans to do so with a three-step strategy, it said: deliver more entertainment value to members; leverage technology to improve all aspects of the service; and improve monetization. Ads on Netflix Central to Netflix's value offering has been its cheaper, ad-supported tier. Yet, the company on Tuesday lowered its full-year revenue guidance for its ad business. Netflix said it now expects 2026 ad revenue of around $2.7 billion, down from the roughly $3 billion the company had previously forecast. That lower guidance is due to a slower-than-expected rollout of some ad product capabilities, the company said. "Our ads business has delivered really impressive growth since we've launched, and we do see a long road of continued growth ahead of us," co-CEO Greg Peters said on the company's earnings call. "We set big growth targets for our ads business this year. We established an aggressive product road map that was consistent with that strategy. And, just note, I think that the build-out that we've been on is the fastest build-out of a comparable ad stack in our industry, but we are currently a bit behind our aggressive target for the year." headlines.article_text: Boeing wins FAA approval for 737 Max 10 after years of delays Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points The FAA certified Boeing's 737 Max 10, the largest model in the best-selling family of aircraft. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told CNBC that the U.S. needs to speed up its certification process In this article BA Follow your favorite stocks CREATE FREE ACCOUNT watch now VIDEO 1:22 01:22 FAA certifies Boeing 737 Max-10 Closing Bell The Federal Aviation Administration on Tuesday signed off on the Boeing 737 Max 10 after years of delays , a major win for the manufacturer and the last in Boeing's best-selling family of jets to get government approval. The green light comes weeks after federal officials reviewed a navigation system glitch on the aircraft but deemed it was not a safety-of-flight issue. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told CNBC's Phil LeBeau that safety is paramount, but he also said the U.S. needs to improve its certification process. "It takes Boeing, to certify an aircraft in Europe, about half the time, less than half the time that it does in the U.S. You have China now playing to take over in aviation," Duffy said. "We have to certify aircraft more quickly if we're going to compete as Americans." watch now VIDEO 5:34 05:34 Watch CNBC's full interview with Transportation Sec. Sean Duffy Closing Bell: Overtime The 737 Max 10, the largest model in the family that can seat up to 230 people, was set to start flying in 2020, but increased scrutiny following two Max crashes in 2018 and 2019 and other safety issues delayed its certification. Engineering changes were also required, including to an anti-icing system for the aircraft's engines. Max 10 customers include Alaska Airlines , American Airlines , United Airlines and Delta Air Lines . Boeing said the Max 10 makes up about 30% of its Max backlog. Airlines can finally start flying passengers soon after planes are certified, but it can take months for carriers to work them into schedules. Alaska Airlines last month said it plans to put lie-flat seats on some of its 737 Max 10s in a push for more premium offerings. The FAA approved the smallest model of the 737 Max family, the Max 7 , in early August. Boeing has been working to ramp up production of its 737 Maxes and 787 Dreamliners, which are key to its recovery since airlines and other customers pay the bulk of the aircraft's price upon delivery.
